newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices mixed, Punjab extend gains.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices mixed, Punjab extend gains.

text.p: Indian Punjab varieties on Monday extended gains while Gujarat cotton held steady at improved levels, dealers said.
Punjab cotton rose on a further shortage of ready stock while reports of dwindling arrivals in the Punjab region kept millers active buyers.
"Arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region fell to 800/1,000 bales (170 kg each) and will slid further in the coming days," one broker said.

In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 25 rupees at 1,700/1,750 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), F-414 by 10 rupees at 1,990/2,010 rupees per maund and Bengal-deshi by 15 rupees at 950/975 rupees per maund.
"Blenders too remained active buyers as the market is witnessing a shortage of medium and superior varieties due to the tailend of the season," he said.

Gujarat varieties on the other hand consolidated recent gains amid limited activity. In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) was steady at 14,000/14,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg), wagad cotton at 12,900 rupees and Kala-ginned at 12,500 rupees per candy.
